title: Test whether code comments help Claude Code build features
summary: Roberto Aranda had Claude Code build two features three times each, with and without 168,000 comment lines; he reports the quality scores were too close to matter.
agent_role: Claude Code implemented the features end to end on both branches, and a separate Claude session blind-scored each change against a checklist. The human designed the experiment, removed the comments, wrote the hidden test and the rubric, and compared the results.
outcome: Author reports that scores were within noise with and without comments, and that one run per branch could have supported opposite conclusions because token use varied from 7.01M to 10.64M on the same task.
what_they_did: Roberto Aranda copied a large WordPress plugin's code and removed about 168,000 lines of comments. He checked both copies produced identical programs. Claude Code with Opus 5.5 built two real features on each copy, three times each, using the same request. He graded results with automatic checks, tests, a hidden test, and a separate Claude session judging each change blind against a checklist.
how_it_went: He reports every run passed every check. Blind scores were nearly the same: 18.3 vs 19.0 out of 19 on the small task, and 21.7 vs 22.0 out of 23 on the bigger one. The small task used about 22% less AI processing without comments. All six bigger-task runs caught a trap where the pinned setting would be lost on reload.
worth_knowing: AI processing on the same task ranged from 7.01M to 10.64M tokens. One run per copy could have made removing comments look 30% costlier or 31% cheaper. Run comparisons more than once. He tested one model and two tasks only.
prompt: Help me test whether [codebase change, e.g. removing comments] affects how well you work in [repo URL]. Create two branches: [main branch] and a copy with [the change applied], and confirm the change doesn't alter behavior. Draft a scoring checklist for the task "[feature description]" and show it to me before any runs. Then implement the feature on each branch [number] times, alternating branches, and record lint, type-check and test results plus tokens used for each run. Label each result with a random name and score them blind against the checklist. Summarize averages and the run-to-run spread, and don't push or open PRs without my approval.

curation.rationale: A controlled, repeatable experiment: Claude Code built two real features three times each on a codebase with and without 168k lines of comments, using blind AI judging, hidden tests, and published PRs, data and scripts. It gives practical, evidence-backed guidance on agent context and run-to-run…
